headline: Daily market snapshot – 2026-10-16
summary: Pre-market and early-Friday composite of major index, rate, commodity, FX, and crypto levels as of October 16, 2026. US futures slightly higher; Asia rebounded; chip selloff continues; Brent ~$107 on Hormuz; gold ~$4,181; BTC ~$82K.
key_facts: KOSPI Oct-16 close +2.05% at 5,668 (week -14.5% worst since Oct-2008)

headline: TSMC Q3 2026: Revenue $46.7B Beats Guidance, Profit +68.7%, Q4 Guide $52.3–54.3B
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor reported Q3 2026 revenue of $46.7 billion, above its $44.6–45.8B guidance, with net income of NT$763B (+68.7% YoY) driven by AI chip demand and 2nm ramp. Q4 guidance of $52.3–54.3B implies ~58% YoY growth. Full-year revenue expected +44% YoY. Despite the beat, Asian chip stocks fell on the day amid broader semiconductor selloff.
key_facts: Operating margin 58.7%; gross margin 66.4% (down 1.3pp from 2nm ramp)
Q4 revenue guide $52.3–54.3B (+58% YoY at midpoint)

headline: Morgan Stanley Q3 2026: Net Revenue $20.3B, EPS $3.03 Beats; Equity Revenue +41% YoY
summary: Morgan Stanley reported Q3 2026 net revenue of $20.3 billion (+11.5% YoY) and EPS of $3.03, beating most consensus estimates on strong equity trading (+41% YoY) and record Institutional Securities revenue of $10.03 billion. ROTCE held above 20% for a fifth consecutive quarter at 22.6%. Shares fell ~2.93% in premarket trading on profit-taking.

headline: Goldman Sachs Q3 2026 EPS $17.01 Beats Consensus by ~30%; Equities Revenue +72%
summary: Goldman Sachs reported Q3 2026 EPS of $17.01, beating the ~$12.86–13.09 consensus by approximately 30%, with revenue of $18.68 billion. A 72% surge in equities trading revenue drove the outperformance. Despite the blowout beat, shares dipped modestly as all major bank stocks fell on earnings day.
key_facts: Shares -0.2% despite strong beat – all banks fell on earnings day
GS beat was largest among the six major banks reporting

headline: Bank of America Q3 2026: $1.2B Regulatory Fine Drives Profit Miss; Shares -5.5%; $32B Market Cap Erased
summary: Bank of America Q3 net income fell to $6.9 billion ($0.91/share) from $8.3 billion a year earlier after a $1.21 billion Treasury/OCC penalty for failing to report $5+ billion in suspicious transactions — the largest OCC penalty in history. Revenue of ~$30 billion missed estimates of ~$30.6B; shares fell ~5.5% erasing approximately $32 billion in shareholder value.
key_facts: $1.21B Treasury/OCC fine for failing to report $5B+ suspicious transactions
OCC portion $750M – largest OCC penalty in history

headline: Citigroup Q3 2026 EPS $2.85 Beats $2.65 Estimate; Profit +40% on Fixed-Income Trading
summary: Citigroup reported Q3 2026 EPS of $2.85, beating the $2.65 consensus as profit rose ~40% on strong fixed-income trading. Revenue of $23.8 billion slightly exceeded forecasts. Despite the beat, Citi shares fell ~2.4%, consistent with the broader bank-earnings-selloff pattern.
key_facts: Profit +40% YoY on fixed-income trading strength

headline: JPMorgan Chase Q3 2026 Rare Profit Miss; Buybacks Cut; EPS $5.57 on Revenue $50.9B
summary: JPMorgan Chase reported Q3 2026 EPS of $5.57 on revenue of $50.9 billion in what Reuters described as a rare profit miss. The bank also announced a reduction in its buyback program. JPMorgan fell on the news.
key_facts: Reuters: one of JPM's rare misses in recent quarters

headline: Wells Fargo Q3 2026 Revenue Miss as Credit-Loss Provisions Rise; EPS $1.87 Beats
summary: Wells Fargo Q3 2026 total revenue was ~$21.87 billion (+2% YoY), missing estimates, while EPS of $1.87 beat forecasts. Higher provisions for credit losses and weaker-than-expected revenue weighed on results despite profit of $5.95 billion.
key_facts: Higher credit-loss provisions weighed on results

headline: BlackRock Q3 2026: AUM Hits Record $15.5T; Adjusted EPS $15.93 Beats by 38%
summary: BlackRock reported record period-end AUM of $15.49 trillion, up 15% YoY, fueled by $205 billion in quarterly net inflows including $135 billion into iShares ETFs. Trailing 12-month inflows reached $869 billion. Adjusted EPS of $15.93 beat the ~$14.13 estimate by 38%; revenue rose 19% to $7.75 billion.

headline: ASML Q3 2026 Revenue €11.66B, EPS €12.95 Beats; Q4 Guide €14.2–15.2B Above Consensus; Stock Falls
summary: ASML reported Q3 2026 revenue of €11.66 billion (up from €7.52B YoY) and EPS of €12.95, beating consensus. Q4 guidance of €14.2–15.2B was above consensus. Gross margin of 57.5% exceeded guidance. Despite the strong report and bullish Q4 outlook, shares fell ~2.9–3.9% as investors remained cautious about chip capex sustainability.

headline: September CPI Accelerates to 3.7% YoY on Energy Surge; Core 2.6%; Fed October Hike Odds Jump
summary: US CPI rose 0.6% in September (3.7% YoY), above expectations and up from 3.4% in August, as gasoline prices jumped 9.1% accounting for more than half of the monthly gain. Core CPI reached 2.6% YoY (above 2.4% prior). The hotter-than-expected print pushed Fed October hike odds from ~22% to ~35–41%.
key_facts: CPI +0.6% MoM, +3.7% YoY (above est; up from 3.4%)
Gasoline prices +9.1% MoM – >50% of monthly increase
Fed October hike odds rose from ~22% to ~35–41%
October FOMC meeting Oct 27–28; December hike odds >90%

headline: September PPI +1.3% MoM (Largest Since March 2022), +6.3% YoY; Inflation Pressure Mounts
summary: US Producer Price Index jumped 1.3% in September, the largest monthly increase since March 2022, taking the annual rate to 6.3%. Released alongside strong retail sales, the data reinforces the case for further Fed rate hikes and compounds inflation concerns following the previous day's hot CPI print.
key_facts: PPI +1.3% MoM – largest monthly gain since March 2022
Released alongside strong retail sales and resilient jobless claims
Compounds hawkish outlook following hot Sep CPI

headline: September Retail Sales +0.8% (Double Estimate); Gas Stations +6.4%; Core Sales +0.1%
summary: US September retail sales rose 0.8%, double the 0.3–0.4% consensus, with gas station receipts surging 6.4% driving most of the headline gain. Excluding autos, sales rose 0.9%. However, core retail sales (ex-autos, gas, building materials, food services) rose only 0.1% vs 0.3% expected, suggesting underlying consumer spending is more modest than the headline implies.
key_facts: Gas stations +6.4% MoM – majority of headline gain
Core retail (ex-autos, gas, building materials, food) +0.1% vs 0.3% est
Not inflation-adjusted; real spending likely lower

headline: Initial Jobless Claims 199K – 5th Straight Week Below 200K; Labor Market Layoffs Contained
summary: Initial jobless claims rose 1,000 to 199,000 for the week ending October 10, slightly below forecasts, marking a fifth consecutive week under 200,000. Continuing claims were approximately 1.71 million. The data contrasts with the weak September NFP (+29K), suggesting that while hiring has slowed sharply, layoffs remain remarkably contained.
key_facts: Contrast: Sep NFP +29K (weak hiring) vs sub-200K claims (low layoffs)

headline: Hot September CPI Pushes Fed October Hike Odds to 35–41%; Year-End Hike >90% Priced
summary: Following the hotter-than-expected September CPI of 3.7%, CME FedWatch showed October 28 Fed hike probability rising to approximately 35–41%, up from ~22% pre-release. Futures price over 90% probability of at least one more hike before year-end. The Fed funds rate currently sits at 3.75–4.00% after the September 2026 hike.
key_facts: >90% probability of at least one more hike before year-end
October FOMC Oct 27–28; next meeting Dec 8–9

headline: China's CXMT Claims 4F² DRAM Breakthrough; SK Hynix -10%, Samsung -7% Day-1 of 6-Session Rout
summary: Chinese memory maker CXMT claimed a 4F² DRAM design breakthrough at a Shanghai conference on October 9–10, promising server DDR5 modules by year-end. The announcement triggered a six-session global chip selloff: SK Hynix -26%, Samsung -22%, Micron -11% cumulatively. CXMT now holds ~10% of global DRAM market. The 4F² architecture could raise memory density 30–50%, though analysts caution mass production is unproven.
key_facts: CXMT claims 4F² DRAM architecture; server DDR5 by year-end
4F² cuts cell area ~33% vs dominant 6F² (30–50% density gain)
SK Hynix -10.09% on Oct 13, -26% over 5 days
Both Samsung (2028 target) and SK Hynix also pursuing 4F²
Analysts: no confirmed mass production; HBM exposure cushions SK Hynix

headline: US Chip Stocks Lose $1.64T Over 6 Sessions; SOX -3.3% Oct 15; On Track for $2T Wipeout
summary: US semiconductor stocks lost approximately $1.64 trillion over six trading sessions, driven by the CXMT 4F² memory threat, hot inflation boosting rate hike expectations, and AI capex sustainability concerns. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell an additional 3.3% on October 15. Nvidia fell ~2.6%, Micron ~3.2%, Marvell ~5%, and ASML ~6.5% in Europe on October 15.
key_facts: $1.64T wiped from chip stocks over 6 sessions
Reuters: stocks on track for $2T total wipeout
Drivers: CXMT DRAM threat, hot CPI/rate hike risk, AI spending concerns

headline: Asia Markets Rebound Oct 16: Nikkei +1.39% at 65,324; KOSPI +2.05% at 5,668 After Circuit-Breaker Session
summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed +1.39% at 65,324 and South Korea's KOSPI closed +2.05% at 5,668 on October 16, bouncing after steep losses the prior session. KOSPI still ended the week -14.5%, its worst weekly performance since October 2008, as Samsung fell ~20% and SK Hynix ~25% on CXMT fears.
key_facts: Samsung -~20% on week; SK Hynix -~25% on week
Circuit breakers triggered on KOSPI/Kosdaq on Oct 15
Prior session Nikkei fell -4.90% – its worst since March 2026

headline: S&P 500 Heads for -1% Week, Nasdaq -2% as CPI, Chip Selloff, and Earnings Compression Weigh
summary: US markets faced a difficult week through October 16 as the S&P 500 fell nearly 1% and Nasdaq shed more than 2% from the prior week close. Technology led losses driven by chip weakness (CXMT threat), hot inflation data raising rate hike expectations, and an earnings-selloff pattern where multiple companies reported beats but still fell, reflecting P/E multiple compression.
key_facts: Earnings beats widely sold: P/E compression theme dominant
Multiple rate hike expectations compress tech growth multiples
CXMT DRAM fears, hot CPI/PPI adding to tech pressure

headline: KOSPI Posts Worst Week Since October 2008: -14.5%; Samsung -20%, SK Hynix -25%
summary: South Korea's KOSPI ended the week of October 16, 2026, down 14.5%, its worst weekly performance since the 2008 financial crisis. Samsung Electronics fell approximately 20% and SK Hynix dropped approximately 25% over the week, driven by fears about Chinese DRAM competitor CXMT's 4F² technology breakthrough in the sixth consecutive day of chip-sector selling.
key_facts: Circuit breakers triggered on KOSPI/Kosdaq on Oct 15 (6th chip-selloff day)
Selloff catalyst: CXMT 4F² DRAM breakthrough claim Oct 9–10

headline: All Six Major US Banks Fall on Q3 Earnings Day Despite Mixed Results; Valuation Reset Underway
summary: Despite a mix of beats and misses, all six major US banks that reported on October 13–14 finished lower on their earnings days. Goldman Sachs beat EPS by ~30% but fell 0.2%; Citigroup beat EPS by 7.5% but fell 5.6%; JPMorgan missed and cut buybacks. Combined NII for JPM, Citi, and WFC was $56.5 billion. Analysts described the results as 'a little bit disappointing' relative to elevated market expectations.
key_facts: All 6 major banks fell on earnings day despite mixed results
GS beat ~30% but -0.2%; C beat 7.5% but -5.6%
JPM missed, cut buybacks; BAC $1.2B fine drove -5.5%
Analysts: results 'a little disappointing' vs elevated expectations
Theme: P/E compression, rate-hike risk, sell-the-news

headline: Brent ~$107, WTI ~$97 as Iran-US Hormuz Standoff Continues; 24 Ships Hit in Two Weeks
summary: Brent crude traded at approximately $105–107.83 and WTI at ~$97.07 on October 16, sustained by ongoing Iran-US tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Hormuz flows are approximately 43% below pre-conflict levels after 24 ship attacks over two weeks. The Brent-WTI spread widened to ~$10, far above the normal $3–5 differential, reflecting concentrated shipping and insurance risk in seaborne Gulf crude.
key_facts: US crude inventory draw ~8.6M barrels supportive
Iran: Hormuz stays closed unless US meets conditions
ING: US-Iran deal could remove geopolitical risk premium

headline: Gold Near $4,181 as Dollar Softens; DXY Slips to ~102; EUR/USD ~1.121; USD/JPY ~158
summary: Spot gold traded near $4,180.60 on the morning of October 16 as dovish Fed commentary and lower Treasury yields pressured the US dollar. DXY slipped toward 102 from a prior-day high of 102.94. EUR/USD held near 1.121 and USD/JPY retreated below 158 in the Asian session as fresh US dollar selling emerged.
key_facts: Dovish Fed commentary and lower yields support gold/yen
Fundamental backdrop still hawkish from hot CPI/PPI

headline: Bitcoin Recovers to ~$82,226, ETH ~$2,450 After CPI Shock Sparked $1B in Liquidations
summary: Bitcoin rebounded to approximately $82,226 (+1.3%) on October 16 after briefly falling below $80,000 following the hot September CPI data, which triggered nearly $1 billion in crypto liquidations. Ethereum recovered to approximately $2,450–2,461 but remained below its 50-day EMA of $2,494. Near-term BTC resistance is seen around $82,500.
key_facts: BTC briefly fell below $80K on CPI shock
~$1B in crypto liquidations on CPI print

headline: Anthropic Targets Post-Midterms November 2026 IPO on Nasdaq; ~$2T Valuation Discussed
summary: Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft S-1 to the SEC and is targeting a Nasdaq listing in November 2026 after the midterm elections, slipping from an earlier fall date. An IPO valuation of approximately $2 trillion has been discussed, based on projected 2028 revenue of $190–200 billion, though the public S-1 has not yet been filed. The company's last private round valued it at $965 billion (Series H, May 2026).
key_facts: S-1 filed confidentially with SEC on June 1, 2026
Discussed IPO valuation ~$2T (based on 2028 rev projections)
Last private valuation $965B (Series H, $65B round, May 2026)
Public S-1 not yet filed on EDGAR as of mid-October

headline: November 2026 Midterms: Pre-Election Market Weakness Historical Pattern; Post-Election Historically Strong
summary: Strategists are previewing November 2026 US midterm elections for market implications. Historically, midterm years average ~1% returns with average intra-year drawdowns of 18%; 12 of 17 midterms since 1957 saw corrections. However, the 12 months post-midterm have typically been strong. The balance of congressional power could materially influence tax and spending policy.
key_facts: Historical midterm years avg +1% return, -18% avg intra-year drawdown
Post-midterm 12 months historically strong for cyclical/growth
Congressional balance of power key for tax/spending legislation
Trump approval ratings flagged as weak entering November vote
